guidance: Write a practical handover for the person who must install, operate and maintain this specific project. Identify whether it is a CLI, library or service before describing deployment. Explain concrete source-supported commands, configuration, inputs, outputs, dependencies and failures. Distinguish documented instructions from verified runtime results. Describe proposed acceptance checks as procedures, not passed tests. Do not invent production URLs, passwords, SLAs, support contacts or deployment infrastructure. If a topic does not apply, explain why briefly rather than requesting unrelated missing information. Repository examples are illustrative, not actual client data.

headings.guidance: Explain the actual product, intended users, delivered components and exclusions. Separate sample business data from this software's purpose.
Describe module responsibilities and at least two supported end-to-end workflows with their inputs, transformations and outputs.
Give supported prerequisites, installation steps and configuration names. Document secret handling without example secret values. Avoid inventing container or cloud deployment.
Describe operator tasks with exact supported commands or interfaces, inputs, expected artifacts and recovery from common errors. Identify destructive or overwrite flags when source establishes them.
Propose concrete smoke checks with prerequisites, action and expected result, grounded in actual commands. Existing test code is evidence of intended checks, not proof that they pass.

Explain source-supported update, backup, dependency and troubleshooting considerations. Distinguish actual implementation limits from decisions the recipient must make; do not invent support arrangements.
